reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch read Noah's words as prophetic insight into the future course of his sons' descendants rather than God instituting or approving slavery as an institution.

discrepancy.note: Ingersoll presses that Scripture makes Jehovah the author of chattel slavery, buying and selling babes, against its own command to love one's neighbor.

quotes.text: But the believer in the inspiration of the Bible is compelled to declare that there was a time when slavery was right—when men could buy, and women could sell, their babes.
quotes.attr: Robert G. Ingersoll (d. 1899), The Christian Religion, pt. III (1881), on Genesis 9:25.

quotes.text: We find that Jehovah, speaking to his chosen people, assured them that their bondmen and their bondmaids must be "of the heathen that were round about them." "Of them," said Jehovah, "shall ye buy bondmen and bondmaids."
quotes.attr: Robert G. Ingersoll (d. 1899), The Christian Religion, pt. III (1881), on Leviticus 19:18.

sides.snippet: Cursed be Canaan; A servant of servants will he be to his brothers.
sides.verseText: He said, \"Cursed be Canaan; A servant of servants will he be to his brothers.\"

sides.snippet: you shall love your neighbor as yourself.
sides.verseText: You shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the children of your people; but you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am Yahweh.
